pr.title: Spec one on-demand daemon that watches pull requests
pr.head: 3bd394a6bd0157bdeff105eb3804cbc58c7a9a24

summary: Projector drives a pull request to a clean review with two background loops today. The watch loop runs in the session that opened a pull request and fixes the review findings that arrive on it. The review loop runs once per repository and reviews every new head of the operator's pull requests. Each loop runs a bash watcher script inside a conversation, and each queries GitHub's GraphQL API for every pull request on every pass, whether or not anything changed.

That design has three costs. The polling spends a GraphQL quota of 5,000 points an hour that every session and machine on the account shares, about 2,000 points an hour at 10 pull requests. Someone has to start each loop by hand. And nothing keeps two review loops on one model from reviewing every head twice.

This pull request adds a plan, not code. One daemon per machine, project watch serve, starts when any project watch command needs it and exits once no session is live. A session subscribes to a pull request in the fix role when it pushes one, and in the review role when it reviews one. The daemon asks GitHub a conditional REST question per pull request, which is free when nothing changed, runs GraphQL only for a pull request that changed, and gives each event to one owning session per pull request and role. In Claude Code, Projector's mod delivers the events as prompts. Both loop skills go away, and a new review-repo skill reviews a repository's pull requests on request.
The plan is at ready with priority now, so it claims that nothing blocking implementation is left open.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Operator: the GitHub account gh is signed in as.
  • Session: one agent conversation with its subagents, named by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in Claude Code.
  • Subscription: a line in a session's subscriptions file naming a pull request or repository and a role, fix or review.
  • Owner: the one live session that receives a pull request's events in a role.
  • Conditional request: a REST request that sends the resource's last ETag, so GitHub answers 304 when nothing changed.
  • Start comment and lock: what project review setup leaves on GitHub and on disk while a review runs.
  • Stall: a review whose lock no command has touched for watch.review_stall seconds, which the daemon then clears.
  • auto line: a fix subscription a push added, which takes no role from an earlier one.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
Earlier heads of this pull request held a different plan, a per-session loop with a review lease, which four reviews worked through. The daemon plan replaced it.

The first review of the daemon plan opened four findings, and all four are fixed:

  • The query carries the panel's row fields, and the pull request body describes the daemon plan.
  • A review role moves between sessions only between reviews, with a 30-minute stall backstop and a fence on publish, move, and settle, so a review left in flight no longer blocks its head for a day.
  • The daemon copies the former owner's record at a move, so the new owner's re-review is accepted.

The latest review is clean. It asks whether 30 minutes is long enough for a live review that waits on the GraphQL quota or on the user, given three recent reviews in this repository that took longer.

groups.title: The watch-daemon plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: a machine-wide daemon, session subscriptions, and per-role owners
intro: The plan follows the repository's plan layout: the problem in § 1, the design in § 2, then the reasons, acceptance criteria, cost, rollout, open questions, and the measurements behind its claims. § 2.1 covers the daemon's life cycle, § 2.2 and § 2.3 sessions and what subscribes them, § 2.4 one pass, § 2.5 ownership, § 2.6 the requests and the query, § 2.7 the events, § 2.8 delivery, and § 2.11 the panel.

Read § 2.5 and § 2.7 most closely. They decide how review work moves between sessions. The review commands keep their state, lock, and start comment per machine and model, not per session, and a session's id becomes the review's loop id.

files.note: The new plan for one on-demand daemon that watches pull requests for every session on a machine.

checks.text: The daemon starts on demand: any command that can take daemon.mutex knows none is running and starts one detached.
Only a version that parses as dotted numbers is compared, so a checkout's unknown never replaces a daemon or is replaced.
--session then PROJECTOR_SESSION matches project inbox, and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in a subagent's Bash command equals its main loop's id.
A push adds an auto line, so pushing one fix to another session's pull request does not take its fix role.

setup takes the lock before it reads --replace, and skips and deletes the start comment this machine's state records. So once the daemon clears the former owner's lock, the new owner's setup succeeds without --replace.

Three of 177 recent Projector reviews in this repository took over 30 minutes: 41 minutes, 1 hour 42 minutes, and 5 hours 4 minutes. A review waiting on the quota reset or on the user may leave its lock untouched long enough to count as stalled.
The query holds every field the panel's row shows: the age from updatedAt and the changed lines from additions, deletions, and changedFiles, as FIELDS in hooks/github.ts reads them.
Standing events repeat every watch.renotify seconds, so a batch lost in delivery comes back, and a stalled review's head comes back as NEW HEAD.
With the former owner's entries copied into the new owner's record, check_collision accepts the new owner's --rereview on a head the former owner reviewed.
The 210-point estimate covers polling only. Reviewers and fixers spend GraphQL of their own.
Every open question is deferred, which is what ready requires.
